slides.title: The field differs from the survey in three ways
slides.text: Distribution shift The field differs from the survey in three ways Corruption The same scene, a worse picture: glare, dust, rain, night, motion blur, a dirty lens. Viewpoint The same road from elsewhere: a pole in place of a vehicle changes scale and angle. Population Other roads: a district with older asphalt, other markings, defects the survey never met. Each has its own test. Corruption and viewpoint can be imitated on frames you already have. A new population can only be collected.

slides.title: Slice before you average
slides.text: The method Slice before you average def by_slice(rows, correct, key): out = {} for value in sorted({r[key] for r in rows}): hit = [c for r, c in zip(rows, correct) if r[key] == value] out[value] = (len(hit), float(np.mean(hit))) return out Every test item carries metadata: lighting, blur, viewpoint, district The result is count and score per value, never the score alone A small slice is a reason to collect, not a finding

slides.title: Could a person name the defect in this crop?
slides.text: Reading errors Could a person name the defect in this crop? Yes, and the model cannot The model has not seen the condition. Data, augmentation or fine-tuning can fix it. No, nobody can The information is not in the picture. Only the camera, the lighting or the time of capture can fix it. Look at sixteen errors of the worst slice before you plan anything. Five minutes of looking decides which of the two you are facing.

slides.title: Annotation guidelines and agreement
slides.text: Session 2 Annotation guidelines and agreement Read boxes and masks in a common annotation format Compute raw agreement and Cohen's kappa between two annotators Revise a guideline from the disagreements and measure again 02

slides.title: A label is a class, a place and a decision someone made
slides.text: Annotation A label is a class, a place and a decision someone made Class One name for the whole crop. Cheap, and enough for a classifier. Box Four numbers around an object. What a detector learns from. A crack's box is mostly road. Mask One decision per pixel. Needed for length and area. Many times the labelling cost of a box. Al-Manar's five crop classes: clear, pothole, longitudinal crack, transverse crack, patch.

slides.title: The same box is written in at least three ways
slides.text: Formats The same box is written in at least three ways Convention A box is COCO x, y of the top-left corner, width, height, in pixels Pascal VOC, torchvision x0, y0, x1, y1 of two corners, in pixels YOLO text files centre x, centre y, width, height, as fractions of the image {"id": 0, "image_id": 0, "category_id": 1, "bbox": [131, 84, 21, 26], "iscrowd": 0} A wrong convention does not raise an error. It trains a detector on boxes that are somewhere else. Draw ten boxes on their images after every conversion.

slides.title: The inspectors want a class the old labels never had
slides.text: A new class The inspectors want a class the old labels never had Alligator cracking: cracks that join into a pattern like crocodile skin. It means the road base is failing, and a patch will not hold. In the old labels each such area was filed under one of the two crack classes, more or less at random. Clearly alligator cracking; two cracks that cross; one closed cell. Which of the last two counts?

slides.title: A guideline is written so that two strangers agree
slides.text: Guidelines A guideline is written so that two strangers agree A definition that can be checked: something to count or measure, not a resemblance Positive and negative examples, with the nearest wrong class beside each The borderline cases named and decided: cut by the edge, partly hidden, two classes at once How to draw: how tight a box, where a mask ends, the smallest object worth a label What to do when unsure: a flag, never a guess

slides.title: Raw agreement flatters a rare class
slides.text: Agreement Raw agreement flatters a rare class Two annotators, 100 crops, a class that appears in about 5. Each says "no" to about 95 They agree on about 90 by saying "no" alike Raw agreement: 90% , and they may not agree on one positive Cohen's kappa kappa = (pobserved − pchance) / (1 − pchance) pchance = P(a says 1) × P(b says 1) + P(a says 0) × P(b says 0) 0 is agreement by chance, 1 is perfect agreement.

slides.title: One rule that can be counted moved kappa from 0.44 to 0.85
slides.text: From the lab One rule that can be counted moved kappa from 0.44 to 0.85 Guideline v1 "Cracks that join into a pattern like crocodile skin." 0.44 kappa, 9 disagreements in 30 crops Guideline v2 "Interconnected cracks that enclose at least three closed cells." 0.85 kappa on the second pass

slides.title: Annotators can agree on what and still disagree on where
slides.text: Label noise Annotators can agree on what and still disagree on where After v2 the two annotators box the same crops One hugs the cracks, one leaves a margin: mean IoU 0.71 between their boxes A detector cannot be more consistent with the labels than the labels are with themselves Label noise has kinds. A wrong class, a loose or shifted box, a missing object. Each one costs a different metric, and an agreement check on a sample is how you find out which you have.

slides.title: What does a low kappa call for?
slides.text: Checkpoint What does a low kappa call for? Two inspectors label 200 crops for "edge break". Raw agreement is 88%, Cohen's kappa is 0.31. What is the next step? Read the crops they disagree on and rewrite the definition Accept the labels, since they agree on 88% of crops Add a third inspector and take the majority vote Ask both to label the 200 crops again, more carefully

slides.title: The survey vehicle films every spot several times
slides.text: Near-duplicates The survey vehicle films every spot several times Three pairs found by a difference hash in lab 1.3. Each pair is one road spot on two passes.

slides.title: A split drawn frame by frame puts one spot on both sides
slides.text: Leakage A split drawn frame by frame puts one spot on both sides 150 of 274 near-duplicate pairs straddle the inherited split (lab 1.3, 1,200 frames) The model is tested on pictures it has, in effect, already seen The test score rises, and the rise is not skill The better a model memorises, the more it gains

slides.title: A difference hash turns a frame into 256 bits
slides.text: Finding them A difference hash turns a frame into 256 bits 1 · Shrink grey, 17 by 16 pixels → 2 · Compare is each pixel brighter than its left neighbour? → 3 · Count bits that differ between two frames → 4 · Threshold 30 bits or fewer: a near-duplicate What it finds and what it misses. The same spot in the same light, shifted by a pixel or two: found. The same spot at night, or shifted by a car's width: missed.

slides.title: Split by road segment, and every frame of a segment moves together
slides.text: The repair Split by road segment, and every frame of a segment moves together def split_by_segment(seg): return ["drop" if s is None else segment_split(s) for s in seg] The split is a function of the segment id, never of the frame It does not rely on the hash having found every duplicate A frame whose segment is unknown is dropped: it is safe on neither side

slides.title: The split report states what is shared: nothing
slides.text: Evidence The split report states what is shared: nothing Split Frames Segments Train 780 44 Validation 130 7 Test 164 9 Dropped, segment unknown 126 Segments in more than one split 0 Near-duplicate pairs across splits 0

slides.title: The leak was worth 33 points to a model that learnt nothing general
slides.text: The price The leak was worth 33 points to a model that learnt nothing general Inherited split 63% Split by segment 30% A one-nearest-neighbour classifier on 16 by 16 grey pixels: it answers with the label of the most similar training crop. It can only memorise. (Lab 1.3, quick pack.) A leaking split rewards the wrong model. It ranks memorisers above models that generalise, so it misleads every choice made with it.

slides.title: Why did the score fall?
slides.text: Checkpoint Why did the score fall? A crack classifier scores 96% with a random split of frames and 81% when whole road segments are held out. Nothing else changed. Which number do you report to the department? 96%: a random split is the standard way to evaluate The mean of the two, about 88% Neither: the model got worse and must be retrained 81%: it is the score on roads the model has not seen

slides.title: Augmentation and what it assumes
slides.text: Session 4 Augmentation and what it assumes Apply one transform to an image, its boxes and its mask together Measure how often a transform changes what the label means Choose augmentations from the conditions the field will bring 04

slides.title: Every augmentation claims that a change does not matter
slides.text: Augmentation Every augmentation claims that a change does not matter Transform The claim it makes Mirror left-right The label does not depend on which side things are Brightness and contrast The label does not depend on exposure Blur The label survives a softer picture Quarter turn The label does not depend on direction Tight random crop Any part of the picture carries the label

slides.title: The pixels, the boxes and the mask move together
slides.text: Mechanics The pixels, the boxes and the mask move together from torchvision import tv_tensors from torchvision.transforms import v2 def apply(transform, img, mask): image = tv_tensors.Image( torch.from_numpy(img).permute(2, 0, 1)) target = tv_tensors.Mask(torch.from_numpy(mask)) image, target = transform(image, target) return (image.permute(1, 2, 0).numpy(), target.numpy().astype(bool)) Tell the library what each input is: image, mask, boxes A geometric transform then moves all of them; a colour transform touches the image only The failure it prevents is silent: a flipped picture with its old boxes

slides.title: Two of six transforms change what the crop shows
slides.text: From the lab Two of six transforms change what the crop shows Mirror left-right 0% Mirror up-down 0% Brightness, contrast 0% Gaussian blur 0% Quarter turn 42% Tight random crop 42% Original, mirrored, quarter turn (now transverse), tight crop (now clear).

(Lab 1.4, quick pack.) Nothing failed loudly. The training ran, the loss fell. Half of the copies of each crack class showed the other class under the old label.

slides.title: Choose augmentations from the conditions the field will bring
slides.text: Choosing Choose augmentations from the conditions the field will bring Start from the failure table Session 1 said: dust, rain, night, blur, pole cameras. Augment towards those: exposure, haze, noise, motion blur, scale and small rotations. Then check each claim Which label could this transform change? How often does it? Measure on a sample with masks before it enters the pipeline. Imitation is not the condition. Darkened daylight is not night. Augmentation narrows the gap; the field test on Day 4 says by how much.

slides.text: Review of Day 1 Which slice goes into the failure note? A field batch is sliced by lighting and viewpoint. The cell "night, pole camera" holds 6 crops and scores 17%; "dust, survey vehicle" holds 38 and scores 21%. What does the failure note say? Night from a pole camera is the worst slice, at 17% The two worst slices average 19% Dust from the vehicle is the worst slice with enough crops; the night cell needs more Slices this small say nothing: report the overall score only

slides.title: Convolutional networks and vision transformers
slides.text: Session 1 Convolutional networks and vision transformers Contrast the assumptions of convolutional networks and vision transformers Fine-tune two pretrained backbones on the same crops Compare two models by condition slice with bootstrap intervals 01

slides.title: Nobody trains a vision model from nothing: start from a backbone
slides.text: Transfer learning Nobody trains a vision model from nothing: start from a backbone 1 · Pretrained backbone trained by someone else on a million or more images → 2 · New head its last layer replaced by one for your five classes → 3 · Fine-tune a short schedule on your own crops What transfers: edges, textures, shapes. A network that has learnt them from a million photographs needs hundreds of road crops, not hundreds of thousands, to learn "pothole".

slides.title: A convolutional network assumes that nearby pixels belong together
slides.text: Family one A convolutional network assumes that nearby pixels belong together Locality Each unit looks at a small window. Edges first, then textures, then parts. Shared weights The same filter slides over the whole image: a crack is a crack wherever it lies. A pyramid Resolution falls and the view widens, layer by layer. These assumptions are true of photographs, so the network does not have to learn them from data. That is why it does well with little.

slides.title: A vision transformer assumes almost nothing and looks everywhere at once
slides.text: Family two A vision transformer assumes almost nothing and looks everywhere at once 1 · Patches a 128-pixel crop is cut into 64 patches of 16 by 16 → 2 · Tokens each patch becomes a vector, plus where it was → 3 · Attention every patch can use every other patch, from the first layer → 4 · Class token one summary vector feeds the head Fewer assumptions, more data. What a convolutional network is given, a transformer must learn, so it depends more on large-scale pretraining and on a careful schedule.

slides.title: A fair comparison fixes everything that is not the question
slides.text: The experiment A fair comparison fixes everything that is not the question ResNet-18 ViT-Tiny Training crops, passes, input size The same: 320 crops, one pass, 128 pixels (lab 2.1, quick mode) Test crops The same 304, from road segments neither has seen Learning rate 0.0003 0.0001 Weights 11.2 million 5.5 million Pretraining data ImageNet-1k ImageNet-21k, then ImageNet-1k The last three rows still differ. You compare two available starting points under one budget. You do not compare two families.

slides.title: The bootstrap asks: how far would this number move on another sample?
slides.text: The interval The bootstrap asks: how far would this number move on another sample? def bootstrap_ci(values, n_boot=1000, seed=0): values = np.asarray(values, dtype=float) r = np.random.default_rng(seed) idx = r.integers(0, len(values), (n_boot, len(values))) means = values[idx].mean(axis=1) return (float(values.mean()), float(np.percentile(means, 2.5)), float(np.percentile(means, 97.5))) values holds one 0 or 1 per test crop Draw the crops again with replacement, a thousand times The middle 95% of the resampled means is the interval It needs no formula, so it works for any metric

slides.title: Overlap means "this test cannot tell", not "these are equal"
slides.text: Reading the table Overlap means "this test cannot tell", not "these are equal" Intervals apart A finding on this test set. Write it down, with the slice and its count. Intervals overlap No evidence either way. Collect more crops of that condition, or pair the comparison. Never "Equally good at night", or "better at night by 25 points". Neither is supported by 16 crops. Slice by condition, because the release question is about conditions. Slicing by class answers another useful question: which defect is hard.

slides.text: Checkpoint How do you settle it? Two backbones are scored on the same 320 test crops. A reaches 88% with an interval from 84% to 91%, B 90% with an interval from 87% to 93%. The department must choose one this week. What is the next step? Bootstrap the difference between the two per crop and read its interval Choose B: it is two points better Declare a tie and choose the smaller model Train both for longer until the intervals separate

slides.text: Session 2 How much to fine-tune Train a linear probe on frozen features Compare a probe with full fine-tuning at two label budgets Decide whether more labels or more training is the next step 02

slides.title: Fine-tuning has three depths
slides.text: How much to train Fine-tuning has three depths Linear probe The backbone is frozen. Only the new last layer is trained: 2,565 weights on a ResNet-18. Partial fine-tuning The last block and the head are trained. The early layers, which hold edges and textures, stay as they are. Full fine-tuning Every weight moves: 11.2 million on a ResNet-18. The deeper you train, the more labels and care it takes. Millions of weights and a few hundred labels can overfit, or forget what pretraining taught.

slides.title: A probe runs the backbone once and trains on what comes out
slides.text: The probe A probe runs the backbone once and trains on what comes out def frozen_features(name, X): model = U.backbone(name) if name == "resnet18": model[1].fc = nn.Identity() else: model[1].head = nn.Identity() return U.predict(model, X, size=128) def linear_probe(F_train, y_train, F_test): mu, sd = F_train.mean(0), F_train.std(0) + 1e-6 clf = LogisticRegression(max_iter=2000) clf.fit((F_train - mu) / sd, y_train) return clf.predict((F_test - mu) / sd) A frozen backbone gives the same output for a crop every time: compute it once The classifier is a logistic regression on 512 or 192 numbers per crop Under half a minute on a laptop for 717 crops It measures how much of the task the pretrained features already solve

slides.title: The table answers the budget question: label more, or train more?
slides.text: Deciding The table answers the budget question: label more, or train more? Train every weight +0.163 Ten times the labels +0.014 On ViT-Tiny, from the probe on 717 labels: train. The compute is minutes; labels cost inspectors' time Then spend labels where the table is weak: glare, dust, rain, night A larger random sample mostly adds daylight The answer belongs to this data. On another task ten times the labels may be worth twenty points. The method transfers; the conclusion does not.

slides.title: Start shallow, and go deeper only when the table says so
slides.text: Choosing a depth Start shallow, and go deeper only when the table says so You have Start with Because Tens of labels per class A linear probe A few thousand weights cannot overfit much, and it runs in seconds Hundreds per class, a task close to photographs The last block and the head Early features already fit; fewer weights to move Hundreds per class, pictures unlike the pretraining data Full fine-tuning at a low rate The features themselves must change: night, dust, a view from above A probe that beats full fine-tuning is a warning about the fine-tuning, not a miracle: too few labels, too high a rate, or too many passes.

slides.title: What does this result tell you?
slides.text: Checkpoint What does this result tell you? On 150 labelled crops a linear probe scores 79%. Full fine-tuning of the same backbone on the same crops, for 30 passes at a from-scratch learning rate, scores 71%. What is the likely explanation? slides.title: The classifier is a list of sentences

slides.title: "Open" is not one thing: code, weights and data each carry terms
slides.text: Licences "Open" is not one thing: code, weights and data each carry terms The code What builds the network. Usually under a permissive software licence. The weights What runs on the roadside unit. Licensed separately by whoever trained them, and often differently. The training data Its terms of access may reach the weights trained on it. The record names it for the legal officer. The library's licence says nothing about a model's weights. One library ships hundreds of sets of weights under a dozen different terms.

slides.title: Terms travel with the weights, and libraries have licences too
slides.text: Two traps Terms travel with the weights, and libraries have licences too Fine-tuning does not wash a licence Weights fine-tuned from non-commercial weights are derived from them. Do not assume they are yours to deploy: choose the starting weights before any training. The detection library Ultralytics publishes its models and code under AGPL-3.0, with an enterprise licence as the alternative. Under the department's rule: a commercial licence, or another library. Run the licence check before the first experiment, not after the best model has been found.

slides.title: Detection and its metrics
slides.text: Session 1 Detection and its metrics Explain how a detector turns score maps into boxes Apply non-maximum suppression and say what it removes Compute average precision at two overlap thresholds 01

slides.title: A detector answers three questions for every object at once
slides.text: Detection A detector answers three questions for every object at once Where A box: two corners in pixels of the frame. What A class: for Rasid, pothole or patch. How sure A score from 0 to 1. Everything downstream depends on where you cut it. Why patch is a class. A repaired pothole is the thing a pothole detector most often takes for a pothole. Teaching the detector to name it is cheaper than filtering it afterwards.

slides.title: Every cell of a grid votes for a class and draws a box
slides.text: How it works Every cell of a grid votes for a class and draws a box 1 · Trunk ResNet-18 turns a 192-pixel frame into a 24 by 24 grid of features → 2 · Score map per cell and class: is the centre of an object here? → 3 · Box map per cell: distances to the left, top, right and bottom edge → 4 · Decode keep cells above a score, turn distances into corners Neighbouring cells see the same pothole. Each draws its own box for it. The raw output holds several boxes per object.

slides.title: Intersection over union is the ruler for "the same box"
slides.text: Overlap Intersection over union is the ruler for "the same box" IoU of two boxes IoU = area of overlap / area covered by either Identical boxes: 1. Boxes that do not touch: 0. A 40 by 40 box against the truth IoU Shifted by 3 pixels each way 0.75 Shifted by 5 pixels each way 0.62 Shifted by 8 pixels each way 0.47 Same centre, 6 pixels of margin all round 0.59 Two common thresholds. At 0.5 a box counts when it is roughly on the object. At 0.75 it has to fit.

slides.title: Non-maximum suppression keeps the best box and drops its echoes
slides.text: Suppression Non-maximum suppression keeps the best box and drops its echoes Top: raw boxes above a score of 0.3. Bottom: after suppression at IoU 0.5. Sort the boxes of one class by score Keep the best one Drop every other box that overlaps it by more than a threshold Repeat with what is left

slides.title: Sort the detections by score and walk down the list
slides.text: The metric Sort the detections by score and walk down the list Score Counts as Precision Recall 0.9 true positive 1/1 1/2 0.8 false positive 1/2 1/2 0.7 true positive 2/3 2/2 Two potholes exist. Each row is the result if the score threshold sat just there A detection is a true positive when it overlaps a still unclaimed truth box by at least the IoU threshold Average precision is the area under precision against recall: here 0.5 × 1 + 0.5 × 2/3 = 0.83

slides.title: A short schedule moved AP at 0.75 far more than AP at 0.5
slides.text: From the lab A short schedule moved AP at 0.75 far more than AP at 0.5 Mean over pothole and patch AP at IoU 0.5 AP at IoU 0.75 Warm checkpoint 0.871 0.306 After two passes over 400 frames 0.894 0.483 Supplied detector, full schedule 0.968 0.785 Report both. AP at 0.5 says the detector finds the objects. AP at 0.75 says its boxes fit. The gap between them names the next problem.

Localisation Class Duplicate Missed Right class, IoU from 0.1 to 0.5 IoU at least 0.5, wrong class Right and fitting, but a better box holds the object A truth box no detection came near

slides.title: Each type points to a different piece of work

Or a lower score threshold Collection and labelling

slides.text: Session 3 Segmenting cracks Compute intersection over union and Dice for masks Fine-tune a segmenter on a short schedule Compare a segmenter with a thresholding baseline by condition 03

slides.title: A box cannot measure a crack; a mask can
slides.text: Segmentation A box cannot measure a crack; a mask can Semantic segmentation One class per pixel: crack or road. Enough for length and area. What Rasid needs. Instance segmentation A separate mask per object: this crack and that crack. Needed to count or follow objects. The cost Masks are the most expensive labels to draw, and thin structures are the hardest to draw consistently. In Al-Manar's frames crack pixels are 1.1% of all pixels. A model that answers "road" everywhere is 98.9% accurate and useless.

slides.title: Down to understand, back up to draw
slides.text: How it works Down to understand, back up to draw 1 · Encoder the same ResNet-18 trunk shrinks the frame to one eighth → 2 · Decoder upsamples step by step back to full size → 3 · Skip connections hand the fine detail of early layers across → 4 · One score per pixel cut at 0.5 for the mask A crack two pixels wide does not exist at one-eighth resolution. Without the skip connections the decoder would have to guess where it was.

slides.title: IoU and Dice count the same three things differently
slides.text: Overlap metrics IoU and Dice count the same three things differently From pixels in both, in the prediction, in the truth IoU = both / (prediction + truth − both) Dice = 2 × both / (prediction + truth) Dice = 2 × IoU / (1 + IoU), so Dice is always the larger. Both ignore the pixels that are road in both masks, which is nearly all of them An IoU of 0.38 is a Dice of 0.55: say which one you report A predicted line one pixel beside a two-pixel crack loses half its overlap

slides.title: Four lines of thresholding are the number to beat
slides.text: The baseline Four lines of thresholding are the number to beat def threshold_baseline(img, k=2.0): grey = img.astype(np.float32).mean(axis=-1) return grey < grey.mean() - k * grey.std() Columns: frame, truth, baseline, supplied segmenter. Rows: day, rain, night. "Dark" is not "crack". The rule also marks potholes, patch seams and shadows, and it finds nothing when the whole frame is dark.

slides.title: The baseline fails where the light changes; the segmenter holds
slides.text: From the lab The baseline fails where the light changes; the segmenter holds IoU on validation frames All Day Glare Dust Rain Night Frames 80 37 13 13 11 6 Thresholding baseline 0.224 0.266 0.072 0.215 0.258 0.008 Segmenter, three passes over 240 frames 0.378 0.408 0.385 0.360 0.368 0.294 Supplied segmenter, full schedule 0.809 0.861 0.740 0.824 0.842 0.618 Six night frames. The night column is the weakest of every row and the least certain. It is the next data request, not a finding.

slides.title: An overlap score needs its object beside it
slides.text: Reading the number An overlap score needs its object beside it The wrong comparison "The segmenter's IoU is 0.6 and the detector's AP is 0.9, so the segmenter is the weak part." Two metrics on two tasks share no scale. The right ones Against the baseline on the same frames. Against the same model under another light. With a tolerance of two pixels. And by looking at twenty masks. For the maintenance team, convert: metres of crack found against metres present is a number they can plan with. IoU is the engineer's number.

slides.title: Why is the overlap low?
slides.text: Checkpoint Why is the overlap low? A crack segmenter scores an IoU of 0.52. Its masks, overlaid on the frames, follow every crack and look about one pixel wider than the labels. What do you report? The model is poor and needs a larger backbone Pixel accuracy, which is 99% and describes the model better The IoU with the object's width, and precision and recall at a two-pixel tolerance Dice, because it is higher for the same masks

slides.title: To count vehicles, you have to know which box is the same vehicle
slides.text: Video To count vehicles, you have to know which box is the same vehicle Al-Manar's four kinds of clip: day, queue, gantry, night. The yellow line is where vehicles are counted.

slides.title: Tracking by detection: link each new box to the track it overlaps most
slides.text: How it works Tracking by detection: link each new box to the track it overlaps most def associate(track_boxes, det_boxes, iou_thr=0.3): iou = U.box_iou(track_boxes, det_boxes) pairs = [] while True: t, d = np.unravel_index(iou.argmax(), iou.shape) if iou[t, d] < iou_thr: return pairs pairs.append((int(t), int(d))) iou[t, :] = -1 iou[:, d] = -1 Every open track remembers its last box A matched detection continues its track An unmatched detection starts a new track An unmatched track waits, then closes

slides.title: One missed detection, and a vehicle becomes two
slides.text: The failure One missed detection, and a vehicle becomes two 49 tracks for 16 vehicles in a daytime clip, with a tracker that has no patience (lab 3.4) The detector misses a vehicle for one frame; its track closes The next detection opens a new track with a new identity An identity switch: the track that covers a true vehicle changes from one frame to the next Two measures, two questions. Count error asks whether the total is right. Identity switches ask whether each vehicle stayed one vehicle.

slides.title: Count a track once, the first time its centre crosses the line
slides.text: Counting rules Count a track once, the first time its centre crosses the line Every crossing Add one whenever a box centre moves from above the line to below it. 14 counted in a queue clip with 13 true crossings Once per track A track counts at its first crossing and never again. 13 counted in the same clip

slides.title: Two settings removed nearly every count error
slides.text: From the lab Two settings removed nearly every count error Kind of clip True crossings Patience 0, minimum hits 1 Patience 5, minimum hits 4 Count error Switches Count error Switches Day 38 3 67 0 1 Queue 39 5 106 0 18 Gantry 39 4 105 0 40 Night 35 14 172 1 6 Patience lets a track survive missed frames. Minimum hits ignores tracks that live two or three frames: the headlight reflections.

slides.title: A right count with broken tracks is ready for counting and for nothing else
slides.text: What the numbers allow A right count with broken tracks is ready for counting and for nothing else Needs the count only Vehicles per hour across one line. The gantry clips count correctly because the line lies beyond the gantry. Needs identities Speed between two lines, turning movements, time spent waiting. Forty switches make each of these wrong. Where the line is drawn is a design decision. Put it where the camera sees clearly. Move the gantry over the line and the counts drop.

slides.title: Is this counter ready?
slides.text: Checkpoint Is this counter ready? On a new camera the tracker reports 52 crossings against 50 true ones, with 3 identity switches. The clips are at dusk, and short tracks appear beside some vehicles. Which change do you try first? Require more hits before a track is counted Raise the patience so that tracks survive longer gaps Count every crossing of the line, not one per track Retrain the detector on dusk frames before changing anything

slides.text: Deployment The model leaves the framework it was trained in Where it was trained Python, a training framework, a notebook with gigabytes of libraries, a graphics processor when one is free. Where it will run Al-Manar's roadside unit: two processor cores, no accelerator, a metered link, a small disk, one frame at a time. An interchange format carries the model across: the network as a graph of standard operations plus its weights, in one file that an inference runtime can execute.

slides.title: Export runs the model once and writes down what happened
slides.text: Export Export runs the model once and writes down what happened example = torch.rand(1, 3, 192, 192) dynamic_axes = { "image": {0: "batch", 2: "height", 3: "width"}, "cls": {0: "batch", 2: "h", 3: "w"}, "box": {0: "batch", 2: "h", 3: "w"}, } torch.onnx.export(model.eval(), example, path, input_names=["image"], output_names=["cls", "box"], dynamic_axes=dynamic_axes, opset_version=17, dynamo=False) The exporter follows one example input through the network By default every size of that example is frozen into the graph Name the axes that must stay free: here batch, height and width model.eval() first: the outputs you compare against must be inference outputs too

slides.title: A copy is proven, not assumed: compare outputs within a stated tolerance
slides.text: Parity A copy is proven, not assumed: compare outputs within a stated tolerance 0.00002 largest difference between the original's and the runtime's raw outputs on eight frames, against a tolerance of 0.001 (lab 4.1) The outputs are never bit-identical: the runtime fuses and reorders operations, and float arithmetic depends on the order State the tolerance before you look Orders of magnitude above rounding means something was exported differently

slides.title: Then compare what the user receives: the boxes
slides.text: Parity, second level Then compare what the user receives: the boxes 1 · Raw outputs score and box maps agree within the tolerance → 2 · Final boxes same count, same class, IoU of at least 0.99 with a partner → 3 · Kept as a test ten frames and their boxes, run on every export From the lab: 30 boxes from the original, 30 from the export, parity 1.000. A tiny difference in a score can move a box across a threshold, so the raw outputs alone do not close the question.

slides.title: The file was right and the prototype still saw potholes everywhere
slides.text: The planted fault The file was right and the prototype still saw potholes everywhere def serve_prototype(sess, frame_bgr): x = frame_bgr.astype(np.float32)[None] x = x.transpose(0, 3, 1, 2) cls, box = sess.run(None, {"image": x}) return U.decode(cls, box, score_thr=0.3)[0] 816 boxes from the prototype on 32 frames where the original reports 30; parity 0.000 The camera library delivers BGR; the model was trained on RGB Values arrive as 0 to 255; the model expects 0 to 1 No exception, no warning. A plausible list of boxes, only a wrong one. Most deployment bugs in vision live in the lines before the model.

slides.title: Write down what the graph does and what the caller must do
slides.text: The contract Write down what the graph does and what the caller must do Step Rasid Who can get it wrong Channel order RGB, outside the graph The serving code Value range 0 to 1, outside the graph The serving code Resize Outside the graph, bilinear The serving code Mean and standard deviation Inside the graph Nobody Decoding and suppression Outside the graph, shared code Whoever copies the settings

slides.title: The parity test fails the day before release
slides.text: Checkpoint The parity test fails the day before release After a runtime upgrade the stored parity test reports a largest difference of 0.004 against a tolerance of 0.001, and 2 of 30 boxes have no partner. The model file did not change. What do you do? Raise the tolerance to 0.01, since 28 of 30 boxes still agree Release with the proven versions, and find what changed before upgrading Release with the upgrade: differences this small are float rounding Retrain the detector with the upgraded library installed

slides.title: Resolution and precision against latency
slides.text: Session 2 Resolution and precision against latency Measure per-frame latency as a median and a 95th percentile Quantise a model to 8-bit integers and re-measure its accuracy Choose an operating point that meets a stated budget 02

slides.title: The roadside unit states its budget before any model exists
slides.text: The budget The roadside unit states its budget before any model exists 60 ms per frame at the 95th percentile, on the unit 2 MB of model file, sent over a metered link 2 processor threads, no accelerator The case's assumption: the unit takes three times as long per frame as the reference laptop. Your table says which settings are worth carrying to the unit, where the real measurement is made.

slides.title: Measure the median and the 95th percentile, after a warm-up
slides.text: Measuring Measure the median and the 95th percentile, after a warm-up def summarise(ms): return (float(np.median(ms)), float(np.percentile(ms, 95))) x = U.to_input(Xv[:1], size) # one frame ms = U.latency_ms( lambda: sess.run(None, {"image": x}), n=100) One frame at a time, as the camera delivers them The first runs are slow: discard them A unit that is fast on average and slow on one frame in twenty drops that frame Name the machine and the number of threads beside every latency

slides.title: Three levers trade accuracy for latency and memory
slides.text: The levers Three levers trade accuracy for latency and memory Lever What it buys What it can cost Input resolution Work falls with the number of pixels Small objects shrink below what the grid can see Numeric precision 8-bit integers: a quarter of the file, faster integer arithmetic Every number moves a little; some models lose accuracy Batch size More frames per second in total Latency per frame: the first frame waits for the last Re-measure accuracy after every change. No rule of thumb says which model loses how much. Only the same validation frames, run again, do.

slides.title: Quantisation maps floats to 8-bit integers, and has to see real frames to do it
slides.text: Quantisation Quantisation maps floats to 8-bit integers, and has to see real frames to do it 1 · Float model weights and activations as 32-bit floats: 3.53 MB → 2 · Calibrate run 32 training frames and record the range of every activation → 3 · Quantise store and compute in 8-bit integers: 0.93 MB → 4 · Re-measure parity is gone by design: measure accuracy again Calibration frames come from the training split and look like the field. Calibrate on daylight only, and the ranges are wrong at night.

Unit latency is the laptop's times three, the case's assumption.

slides.title: The operating point is the most accurate row that meets every limit
slides.text: Deciding The operating point is the most accurate row that meets every limit def choose(table): ok = [r for r in table if r["unit_p95_ms"] <= BUDGET_MS and r["file_mb"] <= BUDGET_MB] return max(ok, key=lambda r: r["ap50"]) \ if ok else None Limits first, accuracy second: a row over the limit is not a candidate From this run: 8-bit at 160 by 160, AP 0.973, about 31 ms on the unit, 0.93 MB No row qualifies is a result too: report it with the nearest row and what would close the gap This table and the chosen row are the evidence for outcome 5. The capstone asks for the same against the budget you state, with the machine named.

slides.title: Does it fit?
slides.text: Checkpoint Does it fit? The budget is 50 ms per frame at the 95th percentile. On the unit, model A has a median of 31 ms and a 95th percentile of 64 ms; model B 38 ms and 46 ms. Model A is one point more accurate. Which do you deploy? Model A: its median is lower and it is more accurate Model A: the mean of its two numbers is under 50 ms Neither, until both are measured again with batch size 8 Model B: it is the only one inside the budget

slides.title: Corruption and shift tests
slides.text: Session 3 Corruption and shift tests Build paired test sets for corruption and camera shift Report the drop per condition with an interval Decide to release, release with conditions or hold 03

slides.title: The pilot fell from 95% to 43% in the field. Will this model?
slides.text: The question from Day 1 The pilot fell from 95% to 43% in the field. Will this model? What the pilot did Trained on clean daylight, tested on clean daylight, and met dust, rain and night for the first time on the roadside. What changes today The field conditions are met in a test, on purpose, before the release. The test decides, and its rule is written first. Three kinds of shift, from Day 1: corruption (rain, glare, night), viewpoint (a moved camera), population (another district). The first two can be imitated on frames you hold.

slides.title: Paired sets: the same road spots under each condition
slides.text: The test sets Paired sets: the same road spots under each condition Rows: clean, rain, glare, night, moved camera. Each column is one test frame, drawn again: frame 17 of the rain set is frame 17 of the clean set, in the rain Each spot is its own control: what differs is the condition, not which potholes were drawn Only test-split segments, at a stated severity Find the frame where the box is gone

slides.title: Report the drop per condition, with an interval on the drop
slides.text: The statistic Report the drop per condition, with an interval on the drop r = np.random.default_rng(seed) vals = [] for _ in range(n_boot): idx = r.integers(0, n, n) # frame numbers vals.append( U.mean_ap([pc[i] for i in idx], [gc[i] for i in idx], 0.5) - U.mean_ap([pf[i] for i in idx], [gf[i] for i in idx], 0.5)) low, high = np.percentile(vals, [2.5, 97.5]) Resample the frames, and use the same drawn frames for the clean and the field score Keep the difference each time The spread of the differences is the interval of the drop Pairing makes it narrower than two separate intervals would be

slides.title: Night costs the most, and its interval is the widest
slides.text: From the lab Night costs the most, and its interval is the widest Condition AP at 0.5 Drop 95% interval of the drop Clean 1.000 Glare 1.000 0.000 0.000 to 0.000 Rain 0.987 0.013 0.001 to 0.035 Moved camera 0.987 0.013 0.000 to 0.042 Night 0.924 0.076 0.022 to 0.159 Lab 4.3, quick mode: the supplied detector on 90 paired test frames, 120 resamples.

slides.title: The release rule is written before the test is run
slides.text: The decision The release rule is written before the test is run Upper end of the drop interval Decision From the lab At most 0.10 Pass Glare, rain, moved camera At most 0.30 Release with a human check: an inspector confirms each detection before a crew is sent Night (upper end 0.159) Above 0.30 Hold: the detector does not run under this condition None The rule uses the upper end, not the estimate. A condition tested on few frames has a wide interval and fails until someone collects more. That is the rule working.

slides.title: "Release" is rarely one word: it is a list of conditions
slides.text: The memo "Release" is rarely one word: it is a list of conditions The release memo, one page The model and its version. The test: 90 paired frames, clean AP 1.000. One row per condition: drop, interval, decision. What happens under each decision, and who does it. What the test did not cover Dust. Motion blur. Districts one by one. Conditions together, such as rain at night. Real cameras. Say so in the memo. Add districts as rows. Results by lighting, weather and district, so that no part of the city is served worse unnoticed.

slides.title: Release, check or hold?
slides.text: Checkpoint Release, check or hold? The rule: pass when the upper end of the drop interval is at most 0.10, human check up to 0.30, otherwise hold. In fog the detector's drop is 0.08 with an interval from 0.01 to 0.33, measured on 25 frames. What is the decision? Hold in fog, and collect more fog frames to narrow the interval Pass: the drop of 0.08 is below 0.10 Release with a human check: the truth is probably in between Pass: with only 25 frames the interval is too wide to count

slides.title: Privacy and monitoring in the field
slides.text: Session 4 Privacy and monitoring in the field Blur faces and plates before a frame is stored and measure what still leaks Define monitors that separate a moved or dirty camera from weather Write the sections of a model card for a vision system 04

slides.title: Street frames hold faces and number plates: blur them before anything is stored
slides.text: Privacy Street frames hold faces and number plates: blur them before anything is stored Top: as the camera delivers them. Bottom: as stored. Drawn frames; no real person or vehicle. A road-damage system has no use for a face or a plate They are personal data, so the pipeline blurs them before storage "Before" is an order of steps: no log, cache, queue or backup sees the raw frame

slides.title: "We blur faces" is a claim until the leak is measured
slides.text: From the lab "We blur faces" is a claim until the leak is measured Blur detections with a score of at least Padding Faces and plates still readable Pixels blurred 0.5 none 29.9% 1.2% 0.5 3 pixels 17.4% 2.6% 0.2 none 16.0% 1.5% 0.2 3 pixels 0.7% 3.2% Two separate causes. Boxes that ran tight, repaired by padding. Detections the detector was unsure of, caught by a lower threshold. Either fix alone leaves one in six.

slides.title: For privacy the operating point is recall, bought with false alarms
slides.text: The operating point For privacy the operating point is recall, bought with false alarms The pothole detector A false alarm sends a crew for nothing; a miss leaves a hole. The two costs are balanced, and the threshold sits in the middle. The face and plate blur A false alarm blurs a patch of wall, which costs the road engineers nothing. A miss stores a readable plate. The threshold goes low. The price in the lab: blurred pixels rise from 1.2% to 3.2% of the frame. For a road department that price is nothing.

slides.title: A monitor that pages for weather is switched off within a week
slides.text: Monitoring A monitor that pages for weather is switched off within a week 12 of 12 cameras raise an alert when the monitor is "brightness left its first-week range" (lab 4.4, 30 days) It rained on three days and every camera went dark together Nothing was wrong with any camera A useful monitor fires on what a technician can fix, and stays quiet otherwise

slides.title: Two monitors, each with a signal, a band and a run length
slides.text: From the lab Two monitors, each with a signal, a band and a run length Monitor Signal Band Run Caught Moved camera Offset of the lane markings, in pixels Within 5 pixels of the installed position 2 days CAM-07 on day 20, one day after the knock Dirty lens Sharpness against the camera's own first week At least 85% of its first-week median 3 days CAM-03 on day 14, five days after the dust began Both stay silent on the three rainy days. Rain darkens a frame; it does not move the lane markings, and it does not last three days.

slides.title: Six things the assessor looks for in the public repository
slides.text: The repository Six things the assessor looks for in the public repository Data card and split report What the data is, the guideline, the agreement score, no site shared across splits. Field-conditions test set Paired with the clean test set, and how it was made. Benchmark table Latency, size and accuracy per operating point, the machine named, the chosen row marked. Model card Results per condition and district with intervals, the privacy controls and their measured recall, the monitors. Release memo One page: release, release with a human check, or hold, per condition, against a rule stated in advance. slides.text: How the repository is scored The rubric Data and splits 20% Model quality and error analysis 25% Latency budget 20% Field-condition tests and privacy 25% Reproducibility 10% A claim without a number is a plan, not a result. And a number without its condition, its count and its interval is half a result.
